q: Why did EcoVadis not credit our energy and emissions figures?
title: EcoVadis: why energy figures got no credit
short: EcoVadis credits energy consumption and greenhouse gas figures only if they cover at least 95% of the scope you are assessed on. Other reported figures need 80%. Numbers for your main plant alone, or a figure typed into the questionnaire with no supporting document, earn nothing.
audience: Indian MSME suppliers with more than one plant or site in their EcoVadis scope

sections.h: The rule in EcoVadis's own methodology
p: Reporting counts only if it covers at least 80% of the scope of assessment, except energy consumption and greenhouse gas emissions, which must cover 95%. A separate rule says only questionnaire answers backed by a document are credited, and the document has to be linked to the right answer.

sections.h: Five reasons a figure gets thrown out
ul: It covers one plant, and your scope includes a second plant, a warehouse or a head office.
It leaves out a fuel: the diesel genset, the LPG furnace or the company vehicles.
The document is a scanned photo. EcoVadis needs machine-readable files with real text, in PDF, DOCX, XLSX, JPG or PNG, under 30 MB.
The document has no date, or does not show it belongs to your company.
The figure is more than two years old. EcoVadis treats reported indicators as valid for two years.

sections.h: Check your coverage before you submit
ol: List every site and entity in your EcoVadis scope, exactly as the questionnaire set-up shows it.
For each site, collect 12 months of electricity bills and every fuel purchase: diesel, LPG, PNG, furnace oil, coal.
Convert them: kWh times the CEA grid factor gives Scope 2; litres or kilograms of fuel times its factor gives Scope 1.
Add up by site and see what share your figure covers. If any site is missing, get its bills before you submit; a partial figure is treated like no figure.
Upload one dated summary that shows the total, the method and the sites covered, and link it to the energy and emissions answers.

example.title: A Rajkot pump-parts maker with two plants, FY 2025-26
lines: Plant 1 grid power: 360,000 kWh x 0.675 kg CO2/kWh = 243.0 t CO2.
Plant 1 diesel genset: 6,000 L x 2.645 kg CO2/L = 15.9 t CO2.
Plant 2 grid power: 150,000 kWh x 0.675 = 101.3 t CO2.
Plant 2 LPG furnace: 4,000 kg x 2.98 kg CO2/kg = 11.9 t CO2.
Company total: 372.0 t CO2. Plant 1 alone: 258.9 t, which is 69.6% of the total.
Reporting Plant 1 only falls well short of 95%, so the figure scores nothing. Both plants together cover 100%.
example.note: Grid factor: CEA CO2 Baseline Database version 22.0 for FY 2025-26. Fuel factors: IPCC 2006 defaults. EcoVadis does not publish how it measures the 95%; share of emissions is a self-check, not its formula.

senseible: Upload a year of bills for every site and Senseible gives Scope 1 and 2 by site with the bill behind each line, so a missing plant shows up before EcoVadis finds it. Its team can then draft the energy and emissions answers from that record for you to review and submit.
